user_text: There's something I've been holding onto for months, and I haven't told anyone.
ai_text: That sounds like a heavy thing to carry alone for that long. What's been the hardest part of keeping it in?

user_text: I still have feelings for a close friend, even though I know they're engaged now.
ai_text: That's such a difficult thing to sit with, caring about someone while also knowing the timing and circumstances aren't yours to change.

user_text: We grew up together, so it feels like these feelings crept in without me really noticing.
ai_text: Feelings built over years of history don't always announce themselves clearly, that makes this even more complicated to untangle.

user_text: I keep telling myself I should create some distance, but then they text me first.
ai_text: It's hard to hold a boundary you've set for yourself when the other person keeps reaching out. What happens for you in those moments?

user_text: We ended up talking until 2am last night, just like we used to.
ai_text: That kind of easy late-night conversation can feel comforting and confusing at the same time, familiar in a way that makes it harder to step back from.

user_text: They mentioned wedding planning in the same conversation where they asked how I was doing.
ai_text: That must have been a strange mix to sit with, being close to their happiness while quietly carrying something else.

user_text: I smiled through the whole call, but afterward I felt completely drained.
ai_text: Putting on a steady face while feeling something different underneath takes a real toll, even when it doesn't show on the outside.

user_text: Sometimes I wonder if they have any idea how much this actually affects me.
ai_text: That's a natural thing to wonder, especially when so much of what you're feeling has stayed unspoken.

user_text: When they don't reply quickly, I catch myself checking my phone every few minutes.
ai_text: That's a really common response when so much emotional weight gets tied to someone's replies. It might help to notice that pattern with some kindness toward yourself rather than judgment.

user_text: I've noticed I don't really enjoy my usual hobbies the way I used to.
ai_text: When so much energy goes into managing complicated feelings, it's common for other things to feel flatter than they used to. Has anything still managed to bring you a little joy lately?

user_text: Not really. Most evenings I just end up replaying our conversations instead.
ai_text: That replaying can feel like it's helping you understand things, but it often just keeps the same feelings in motion. What would it look like to give yourself a break from that tonight?

user_text: I don't know how to stop hoping for something that probably isn't going to happen.
ai_text: Hope like that doesn't just switch off because it isn't realistic, it takes time and often some grieving of what you wanted instead. You're allowed to feel this without rushing yourself past it.

user_text: Do you think I'm a bad person for feeling this way?
ai_text: Not at all. Feelings don't make you a bad person, they're not something you chose. What matters is how you act on them, and it sounds like you've actually been quite thoughtful about that.

user_text: I think I just needed someone to hear all of this without judging me.
ai_text: I'm really glad you shared it. Carrying something like this alone is so much heavier than carrying it with even one person who understands.

user_text: Thank you. I feel a little more at peace just having said it out loud.
ai_text: That's a meaningful shift, even if the situation itself hasn't changed yet. Being honest with yourself about it is often the hardest and most important part.
